title: In vitro co-culture of human intestinal organoids and lamina propria-derived CD4+ T cells
protocol: Remove the mesothelium surrounding the intestine.
Cut the intestine open longitudinally if necessary.
Remove the muscular layer in case of pediatric and adult tissues.
Cut intestinal tissue into 0.5×0.5 cm segments.
Wash the tissue segments by shaking in PBS until faeces is removed and the supernatant is clear.
Remove PBS and distribute the tissue pieces in wells of a 6-well plate.
Add 5 mL EDTA/DTT mix per well and incubate for 1 hour at 4°C on a shaker (400–600 rpm).
Vigorously pipet the tissue pieces up-and-down 20 times with a 25 mL serological pipette.
Filter the collected supernatant through a 70 μm cell strainer in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Spin the filtered cells at 500 g and 4°C for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL AD+.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Spin the tube at 500 g and 4°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the final pellet in the appropriate volume of AD+ and transfer to a pre-cooled 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Mix the cell suspension with Matrigel at a ratio of 1:2 (add 20 μL Matrigel per 1/24 well).

Avoid creating bubbles in the Matrigel; slowly pipet the Matrigel on top of the pellet by ejecting the Matrigel against the wall of the tube above the cell pellet, do not go past the first stop on the pipet.
Turn down the volume of the pipet to 50% of the Matrigel-cell suspension volume and gently mix by slowly pipetting up-and-down without going past the first stop on the pipet.
Seed 3 drops of 10 μL per well in a pre-warmed 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate for 10 minutes at 37°C.
Add 500 μL HISC+Y per well and culture at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Change the medium every 2–3 days.
Switch to Y-free medium the first time the culture is refreshed.
Passage organoids after 5-10 days, depending on growth rate.
Resuspend the pellet in just enough AD+ until it is no longer too viscous to pipet with a P20 tip.
Seed organoid cultures into wells based on tissue size and availability.
Pre-warm 24-well plates for at least 1 hour in the incubator at 37°C.
Thaw Matrigel on ice until it is liquid enough to pipet, always keeping Matrigel at 4°C during this protocol.
Store unused Matrigel at -20°C and maintain its temperature below 8°C until culturing organoids in the incubator.
Combine all tissue pieces left over after detachment of epithelial cells in one well of a 6-well plate.
Mince the tissue with scissors and transfer to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 15 mL Collagenase D mix to the minced tissue.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C on a shaker at 100 strokes per minute.
Collect the supernatant and filter through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Spin the tube with the cell suspension at 500 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells with PBS, then place on ice.
Resuspend any remaining tissue pieces in 15 mL fresh Collagenase D mix.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C on a shaker at 100 strokes per minute.
Collect the supernatant and filter through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Pool the cells and spin at 500 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells with PBS.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL HBSS.
Layer the cells on 4 mL standard isotonic Percoll solution (SIP).
Centrifuge the cells for 20 minutes at 18°C–22°C and 1000 g.
Collect the lymphocyte ring.
Wash the cells twice with PBS.
Count the cells using a Bürker chamber.
Exclude dead cells with 0.4% Trypan Blue.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ice-cold FBS.
Add an equal volume of ice-cold FBS + 20% DMSO dropwise to reach a final concentration of 10% DMSO.
Transfer cells to a cryovial.
Freeze the cryovials in a StrataCooler at -80°C.
On the next day, transfer the frozen cryovials to a liquid nitrogen tank.
Change the HISC medium of the organoid cultures every 2–3 days.
Remove the medium carefully without disturbing the Matrigel droplets.
Ensure fresh medium is at 18–22°C before adding to the cultures.
Add Y to HISC immediately after seeding organoids or turning cultures into single cells using TrypLE.
Switch to HISC without Y with the next refreshment of medium.
Passage organoid cultures every 5-7 days depending on growth.
Monitor the density of organoid cultures closely as there is donor-to-donor variation in growth rates.
Split cell cultures based on density, usually splitting one well into four new wells each week.

Judge ideal density during normal culture by microscopy; organoids should be close together and touching but not overlapping between 30-40 organoids per 10 μL Matrigel droplet at a passaging ratio of 1:4.
Avoid too dense seeding of organoids as it leads to faster differentiation, darkening, and loss of round cystic appearance.
Pipette 1 mL ice-cold AD+ into a 15 mL centrifuge tube per culture and keep on ice.
Remove the medium from each well.
Harvest the organoids by liquefying the Matrigel with 1 mL ice-cold AD+ per well and transfer into a 15 mL centrifuge tube (maximum of 8/24 wells per 15 mL centrifuge tube).
Fill the tube up to 14 mL with ice-cold AD+.
Centrifuge for 5 mins at 200 g and 4°C.
Remove the supernatant with a 5 mL serological pipet and P200 tip, removing as much medium as possible including any Matrigel on top of the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL AD+.
Mechanically disrupt the organoids by pipetting multiple times (20 repetitions) with a P1000, followed by disruption with a P200, and then a P20 tip.
Check organoid fragments under a microscope to confirm they are disrupted.
Repeat mechanical disruption until organoids no longer appear round and cystic but rather like shards.
Top up to 14 mL with ice-cold AD+.
Centrifuge for 5 mins at 200 g and 4°C.
Remove the supernatant with a 5 mL serological pipet and any remaining medium with a P200 tip.
Resuspend the pellet in the appropriate volume of AD+ and transfer to a pre-cooled 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Per 1/24 well, use 10 μL AD+.
Mix the cell suspension with Matrigel at a ratio of 1:2 (add 20 μL Matrigel per 1/24 well).
Seed 3 drops of 10 μL per well in a pre-warmed 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate for 10 mins at 37°C.
Add 500 μL HISC per well and culture at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Change medium every 2–3 days.
Passage organoids every 5–7 days.
Thaw cells at 37°C in a water bath until a pea-sized clump of ice remains.
Transfer cell suspension to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 20 mL of ice-cold IMDM with 30% FBS dropwise while shaking the tube.
Mix well by pipetting.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 500 g and 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet twice with PBS, keeping on ice.
Count live cells using a Bürker chamber and 0.4% Trypan Blue solution.
Resuspend LPL in FACS buffer.
Determine cell count using a Bürker chamber.
Pellet cells at 400 g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Prepare the antibody-mix to stain CD4+ T surface molecules.
Keep the antibody mix on ice and in the dark until further usage.
Resuspend 10 million mononuclear cells per donor in the antibody mix using 100 μL antibody mix.
Incubate the resuspended LPL with the antibody mix for 30 minutes at 4°C, in the dark, and shaking at 600 strokes/min.
Wash the cells by adding 1 mL FACS buffer to the suspension per 100 μL antibody mix used.
Pellet the cells at 400 g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant after pelleting the cells.
Repeat step 73 (wash the cells again) to reduce background fluorescence.
Resuspend the washed cells in FACS buffer at a maximum of 25 million cells/mL.
Acquire the labeled mononuclear cells on a FACS-sorter using the gating strategy described.
Sort viable CD45+CD3+CD4+CCR7-CD45RA- Tem cells into tubes filled to at least 10% with T cell medium.
Pellet the cells at 400 g and 4°C for 5 mins.
Remove the supernatant.
Pool the tubes if required.
Use T cell medium.
Resuspend the sorted cells in T cell medium at 4 million cells/mL.
Prepare 2× stimulation medium by adding anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 to T cell medium according to specified concentrations.
Combine the cells suspended in T cell medium with 2× stimulation medium in equal volumes to achieve an end concentration of 2 million cells/mL in 1× stimulation medium.
Incubate the cell suspension for 2 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Liquefy the Matrigel using 800 μl ice-cold AD+ per well.
Transfer the organoids in suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Fill each tube containing the organoids up to 14 ml with ice-cold AD+.
Pellet the organoids at 200 g and 4°C for 5 mins.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 200 μl TrypLE to the pellet and resuspend.
Manually shake in a water bath (37°C) for 2 min, then pipet up-and-down 20 times using first a P200 and then a P20 tip.
Inspect the digestion under the microscope.
Repeat the TrypLE treatment with fresh TrypLE until >95% single cells are observed or after a maximum of 4 rounds.
Add 10 ml AD+ with 10% FBS per tube containing organoids to inactivate the TrypLE.
Incubate at 18°C–22°C for 5 mins.
Pellet the cells at 400 g and 4°C for 5 mins, then remove the supernatant.
Add up to 14 ml ice-cold AD+ to each tube.
Repeat the pelleting step.
Resuspend the cells in ice-cold AD+.
Count the total number of single cells in the organoid cell suspension with a Bürker chamber.
Take 10,000 single organoid cells (3333 cells/droplet) per half well and keep them in AD+ on ice.
Resuspend sorted activated CD4+ Tem cells in AD+ at a concentration of 90 cells/μL (3× the desired end concentration).
Pellet the appropriate number of intestinal organoid single cells suspension (10,000 single cells per 1/24 well) at 400 g and 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the single organoid cell pellet in AD+ harboring 90 CD4+ Tem cells/μL and transfer to a pre-cooled microcentrifuge tube.
Per 1/24 well, use 10 μL of AD+ with resuspended T cells at 90 cells/μL and single organoid cells at 1000 cells/uL.
Mix the cell suspension with Matrigel in a ratio of 1:2 (add 20 μL Matrigel per well).
Seed 3 drops of 10 μL mixture per well in a pre-warmed 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate for 10 minutes at 37°C.
Add 500 μL HISC+Y-SB+IL-2 to each well and culture at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium every 2–3 days, switching to Y-free medium during the first change.
Track organoid development using a microscope starting from day 5.
Incubate T cells with CellTrace Violet.
Visualize T cells by microscopy.
Image each Matrigel droplet containing organoid-T cell co-cultures.
Count the number of organoids per field of view.
Determine the size of individual organoids using ImageJ software.
Use the ‘Multi-point tool’ and ‘Measure’ features in ImageJ for quantification.
